inputs: Workforce records: CoverageReport, CapabilityGap, CapabilityPerformance, RoleNecessityReview, OrganizationalDebt
ResourceUsageRecord or ResourceSummary, a research BatchReport shape, and org_registry.yaml manager edges
ExperimentResult and AnalyticsLearning, read as evidence that work is producing learning rather than only output
invariants: Advisory only: no module writes org_registry.yaml, permissions.yaml, constitution.md or the agent contract schema.
A recommendation never approves itself; APPROVED needs a Decision naming a person who is not an automatic marker.
An ordinary optimisation may not touch no_subagents, the mission, the constitution or CEO authority (rule 2).
No company, department, manager or employee score exists; dimensions stay separate (brief section 4).
Every signal and finding carries an explicit window; an unmeasured value stays None and names what is missing.
A finding needs evidence and at least one signal; a post-change review can never claim causality.
Workforce, usage and research numbers are consumed, never recomputed (rule 15).
The store refuses a silent overwrite: different bytes under one id raise unless replace=True.
purpose: Reads evidence the other subsystems produced and answers whether the company is organized well: signals, then findings, then evidence-backed recommendations and change proposals a human decides on. It recommends; it never reorganizes.
risks: The research BatchReport is read duck-typed, so an upstream rename raises rather than silently yielding None.
Reserved-action mapping reads permissions.yaml ceo_reserved; unreserved_actions reports a rename, it cannot prevent one.
Span, depth and recurrence thresholds are opinions; a finding is only as defensible as the configuration recorded beside it.
The delegation model it reads is advisory in shadow; a vacancy or a conflict it reports is a finding about the chart, not an approval.
title: Organizational intelligence and change proposals
